The one action that clears it is a maintainer adding the yearless filename candidate in report_url of scripts/gridwatch/queue_collect.py, then CI can go green and PR 456 can merge.
  • Shipped at the round cap at 6.868, 1.132 under the 8.0 top rung. Named in all three rounds and not fixed: the dog reads as a smooth figurine at native size, frame 5's monitor and keyboard read as primitives, frames 6 and 7 read as two grids back to back, and the close lands softly.
  • Frame 5 closes the c4 quote with the full stop inside the marks where the source sentence continues. Found in round 3, past the cap, where only a hard fail may be repaired.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it A phone on a vehicle window will survey San Antonio's loose dogs, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

How a stray looks is spelled out.

Southwest Research Institute's release says strays "appear to be malnourished and skittish". Dogs that seem healthier and more approachable "are likely owned by local families and are classified as roaming."

In San Antonio a phone on a vehicle window will record video. Object detection software will find the dogs. Automated and human review will check that each dog was unrestrained. The same review will assess whether it was owned or a stray.

The project will repeat a 2019 manual survey in the same 32 study areas. It is a sample, not a count of every dog.

Animal Care Services Director Jon Gary calls the study another tool for seeing where loose dogs turn up. Field research is expected to run through December. The department will get a final report.

Will the report say how often a person and the software disagreed?

#SanAntonio #SAACS #SwRI

The machine changed itself

  • The grid page's monthly queue chart scrolls inside its own box on a phone (scripts/site/theme.py)
    At ten months it ran 42px past a 320px screen, the responsive step red on main
  • Three machine queue items: street_dog and window_phone built in the chassis, the kit monitor read as primitive, a camera space occluder that kept an old fov
    Named across panel rounds and pixel rounds this run, queued for the weekly pass
  • Two instincts: place occluders from the camera's own fov, and read every sentence's tense and actor against its claim before the panel
    Round 1's integrity judge scored claim integrity 5.5 on tense and attribution, and 8.0 the next round once fixed

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

NOT MERGED. PR 456 is open and ready, and CI is red on gridwatch_pagecheck (exit 3), as on main. The large load queue reading has been stopped since October 16th, because ERCOT now publishes the Monthly Operational Overview with no year in the filename and queue_collect.py builds the name with the year. The one action that clears it: add the yearless filename candidate in report_url of scripts/gridwatch/queue_collect.py (cron lane, a maintainer's change). The image links below point at the run branch until it merges. The deck shipped at the round cap at 6.868, 1.132 under the 8.0 top rung, with no hard fail in any round. Rounds were 6.546, 6.936 and 6.868. Round 1's integrity judge charged the copy for flattening the release's future tense and giving the review's checks to software alone, and all of it was fixed before round 2. Named in all three rounds and not fixed: the dog reads as a smooth figurine at native size, frame 5's monitor is a primitive, and frames 6 and 7 read as two grids back to back. Frame 5 also closes its quote with the stop inside the marks, found past the cap. The record: tx-2026-0236 admitted on the SwRI release and the City of San Antonio release. Its summary was corrected to the release's tense and attribution after the judges read it. tx-2026-0237 and tx-2026-0238 are held for a primary record. Re-verify confirmed 10 items and left 11 with a dated unconfirmed line. Permissions: prompt_audit measured 1,747 calls and listed 45 that waited, the longest a SendMessage at 30.9 s and an Agent launch at 19.5 s, with nobody present. These are dispatch latency as the machine queue item prompt-audit-counts-agent-latency describes, now at repeat 3. The no-stall hook was armed at 05:03:24Z, judged the session unattended from the start (the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED was 0) and refused nothing.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
